intro: Match each enduring issue umbrella to what it's about. These are the words on our classroom posters.

left.label: Power & Its Abuse
hints: Which choice is about who's in charge?

left.label: Identity & Nationalism
hints: Which choice is about who people are?
Look for "who a people say they are."

left.label: Wealth & Resources
hints: Which choice is about owning and producing?

left.label: A Connected World
hints: Which choice is about faraway places?

right.label: Who holds authority, and what happens to the people who did not choose them.
Why people fight, and what is still unsettled when the fighting stops.
Who a people say they are, and who that leaves out.
Who owns what a place produces, and who does the producing.
What new tools let people do, and what they cost the world around them.
What happens when distant places start depending on each other.

rationale.a: Power & Its Abuse asks who holds authority and what happens to people who didn't choose them. Louis XIV's nobles and Catherine's serfs are examples.
rationale.b: Conflict asks why people fight and what's left unsettled after. Hobbes feared a war of everyone against everyone.
rationale.c: Identity & Nationalism asks who a people say they are, and who that leaves out. Aurangzeb's treatment of Hindus is an example.
rationale.d: Wealth & Resources asks who owns what a place produces and who does the work. Serfs worked land they didn't own.
rationale.e: Technology & Environment asks what new tools let people do and what they cost the world around them.
rationale.f: A Connected World asks what happens when distant places depend on each other, like Europe's trade with the Mughal Empire.
